1.note: Qoheleth is speaking of his own thoughts as if they were a person that he could talk to, his **heart**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I thought to myself]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **joy**, you could express that idea in another way. Also, Qoheleth is speaking of **good** as if it were a thing that he could **see**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [by making you glad and letting you experience what is pleasant]
Qoheleth is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. See how you translated this word in 1:14.
See how you translated this word in 1:14.

2.note: Qoheleth is speaking **To laughter** and **to joy** though he knows they cannot hear him. He is doing this to communicate to the people listening that he feels very strongly about these emotions and their place in life. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words as if he were speaking directly to the people about them. Alternate translation: [About laughter, I said, “Madness!” And about joy]

Qoheleth is using a word that expresses a strong feeling of scorn. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [Ridiculous]

Qoheleth is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [And to joy, I said, “What is this doing]

Qoheleth is using the question form to show that pleasure accomplishes nothing worthwhile. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [This accomplishes nothing!]

3.note: Qoheleth is using **to drag my flesh with wine** as a common expression of the culture to mean “to gratify my body with wine.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to gratify my body with wine]

Qoheleth is speaking of his **heart** as if it were a living thing that could guide him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I was still thinking wisely all the while]

Qoheleth is speaking of **folly** as if it were an object that he could take hold of with his hand. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and to take up foolish behavior]

Here the masculine term **sons** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. See how you translated the same phrase in 1:13.

Qoheleth is using **under the heavens** as a common expression of the culture to mean “here on the earth during this life.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase in 1:3 Alternate translation: [here on the earth]

4.q: בָּנִ֤יתִי לִ⁠י֙ בָּתִּ֔ים נָטַ֥עְתִּי לִ֖⁠י כְּרָמִֽים
4.note: Qoheleth is using **I built for myself houses** and **I planted for myself vineyards** to represent the work that he had others do for him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I had houses built for myself. I had vineyards planted for myself]

5.note: The term **royal parks** describes large, enclosed gardens that belonged to a king. If your readers would not be familiar with what royal parks are, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [and large walled gardens]

Qoheleth is using the possessive form to describe a **tree** that is characterized by the kind of **fruit** that it bears. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [every kind of fruit tree]

7.note: Qoheleth is using **sons of the house** as a common expression of the culture to mean “servants who were born in my household.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and servants born in my household]

Here the expression **to my face** means “before me” (in time). If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language here and throughout this chapter. Alternate translation: [before me]

8.note: Qoheleth is using the possessive form to describe **treasure** that is characterized by belonging to **kings and provinces**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the treasure that kings and provinces possessed]

Qoheleth is using **breast and breasts** to represent women. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [an abundance of women] or [many women for myself]

9.note: Qoheleth is speaking of his **wisdom** as if it were a living thing that could stand beside him as a companion. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I remained wise through it all]

10.note: Qoheleth is speaking of the enjoyment that he received from his work as if it were a **portion** of land or food that had been assigned to him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and this was what I received in return for all my toil]

11.note: Here, **my hands** represents my own efforts. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [that I had accomplished by my own efforts]

Qoheleth is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of expressing this. Alternate translation: [and to the work that I had labored to accomplish]
See how you translated the same expression in 1:14.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **profit**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and nothing under the sun benefited me]

12.q: מֶ֣ה הָ⁠אָדָ֗ם שֶׁ⁠יָּבוֹא֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י הַ⁠מֶּ֔לֶךְ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר כְּבָ֖ר עָשֽׂוּ⁠הוּ
12.note: Qoheleth is using the question form to emphasize that whoever comes after him will not be able to do anything more than what has already been done. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [the person who will come after the king can do nothing more than what has already been done.]

Qoheleth is not referring to a specific **person**. He means people in general who might come after him. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [what can any person do who will come after the king]
Qoheleth is speaking of himself in the third person as **the king**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [after me]

13.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **the light** is more useful than **the darkness** for seeing where one is going, so wisdom is more useful than folly for living well. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [as light helps a person to see where he is going, but darkness does not]

14.note: Qoheleth is using the expression that **his eyes are in his head** as a common expression of the culture to mean “he sees where he is going.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The wise, he sees where he is going]

Qoheleth is speaking of the way a foolish person lives as if it were **walking** in **the darkness**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [but the fool lives without understanding]

Qoheleth is using a construction in which a verb and its subject come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. The implication is that the one **happening** that will happen to both of them is death. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternatively, your language may have another way of expressing this. Alternate translation: [that the same thing will occur to both of them] or [that one thing, namely death, will happen to both of them]

15.note: Qoheleth is using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of dismay. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [Alas, the very thing that happens to the fool will happen to me too]

Qoheleth is using the question form to express his frustration that becoming **wise** gained him no lasting advantage. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [And so I was exceedingly wise for no reason at all!]
If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as a direct quotation. Alternate translation: [And I said to my heart, “This also is vapor.”]

16.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **memory**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [people do not remember the wise person]

The expression **forgotten** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [no one will remember either of them]

Qoheleth is using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of grief. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [How terrible! The wise die with the fool]

17.note: The expression **was done** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [was the work that people did under the sun]

18.q: אֶת כָּל עֲמָלִ֔⁠י שֶׁ⁠אֲנִ֥י עָמֵ֖ל תַּ֣חַת הַ⁠שָּׁ֑מֶשׁ
18.note: Here, **my toil** represents what I had gained by my toil. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all the possessions that I had earned by my hard work under the sun]

19.q: וּ⁠מִ֣י יוֹדֵ֗עַ הֶֽ⁠חָכָ֤ם יִהְיֶה֙ א֣וֹ סָכָ֔ל
19.note: Qoheleth is using the question form to emphasize that no one is able to know the answer. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [And no one knows whether he will be wise or a fool.]

The pronoun **he** refers to the person who will come after Qoheleth, whom he mentions at the end of the previous verse. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Will that person who comes after me be wise or a fool]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **authority**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And he will rule over all my toil]

21.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **wisdom** and **knowledge** and **skill**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [is that of someone who is wise, knows much, and who possesses skills]

22.q: כִּ֠י מֶֽה הֹוֶ֤ה לָֽ⁠אָדָם֙ בְּ⁠כָל עֲמָל֔⁠וֹ וּ⁠בְ⁠רַעְי֖וֹן לִבּ֑⁠ו שֶׁ⁠ה֥וּא עָמֵ֖ל תַּ֥חַת הַ⁠שָּֽׁמֶשׁ
22.note: Qoheleth is using the question form to emphasize that nothing lasting comes to a person from all his hard work. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [For nothing endures for the person in exchange for all his toil and the striving of his heart with which he labors under the sun.]

23.note: Qoheleth is speaking of a person’s **days** as if they were **pains** and of his **anger** as if it were **business**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all his days are full of pain, and his work causes him grief]
If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **anger** and **business**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [and he works angrily]

24.note: Here the masculine term **he** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [There is nothing better for humanity than that he or she should eat and drink]

Qoheleth is using **cause his spirit to see good** as a common expression of the culture to mean “find enjoyment.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and enjoy himself in his toil]
Here, **the hand of the God** represents what God gives. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [is what God gives]

25.q: כִּ֣י מִ֥י יֹאכַ֛ל וּ⁠מִ֥י יָח֖וּשׁ ח֥וּץ מִמֶּֽ⁠נִּי
25.note: Qoheleth is using the question form to emphasize that no one is able to eat or to enjoy anything apart from God. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [for no one can eat or enjoy anything apart from him!]

Some ancient manuscripts read “apart from him.” The ULT follows that reading. Other ancient manuscripts read “apart from me.” If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT.

26.note: Here, **to his face** represents in his judgment. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [who is good in his judgment]
The pronoun **he** refers to God, whom Qoheleth names later in this verse. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [God gives wisdom and knowledge and joy]

The terms **gathering** and **collecting** mean similar things. Qoheleth is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [of amassing wealth]
